key_insight: XCAPE combines powder X-ray diffraction constraints with machine-learning-guided crystal structure search to recover physically plausible atomic structures.
engineering_relevance: The framework could accelerate diffraction-based materials characterization and support automated materials discovery workflows.
method: Use composition, unit cell, space group, and PXRD data to constrain a symmetry-aware evolutionary search.
Explore Wyckoff-site configurations with tailored mutations and evaluate energy and diffraction agreement.
Accelerate geometry optimization with a universal machine-learning interatomic potential.
evidence_signal: XCAPE recovered 71/77 simulated-pattern benchmarks and 12/12 experimental reference structures; among 12 additional candidate assignments, DFT placed 10 within 10 meV/atom of the convex hull.
watch_item: Diffraction agreement and low predicted energy do not establish a unique structure, so unresolved candidate assignments need independent validation.
paper_title: Physics-Guided Crystal Structure Elucidation from Powder X-Ray Diffraction with Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
